rules: Official dataset page readback reports 2,595,903 title-boundary entities.
Official dataset page reports one data provider.
Official dataset page reports collector last ran 2025-11-26.
Official dataset page reports new data last found 2025-11-26.
Dataset origin notice says some data was created by MHCLG and authoritative replacement work is ongoing.
Dataset licence is Open Government Licence v3.0.
Attribution states HM Land Registry copyright/database rights 2026.
Polygon geometry attribution states Ordnance Survey copyright/database rights 2026.
Coordinate search requires latitude and longitude and returns entities whose geometry intersects the point.
Multiple dataset parameters may be supplied in one coordinate request.
UPRN search uses q and is described as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point among other fields.
Documentation warns absence of results does not prove absence of constraints because coverage varies.
Custom spatial queries accept WKT geometry.
Spatial query coordinates are WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Pagination uses offset together with limit.
Response links include next, prev, first and last URLs.
The API has no batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
Documentation recommends one request per property with polite rate limiting.
Bulk downloads are available in CSV, JSON and where applicable GeoJSON and Parquet.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source HM Land Registry dataset.
INSPIRE contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry's wider freehold Index Polygons database.
INSPIRE files are divided by local authority.
A polygon on a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
Polygons show position and indicative extent rather than definitive legal extent.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.
HM Land Registry directs users to Find a Property using the INSPIRE ID for title registration and plan information.
Registered-title extent can only be identified from the individual title plan, not INSPIRE alone.
One title number may contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Missing INSPIRE ID may indicate unregistered land, leasehold registration or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
Business e-services MapSearch exposes the full Index Polygon dataset to eligible customers.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence.
The public download page states the current published release is 5 July 2026 and new files are published on the first Sunday of each month.
Layer 0 is named LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Extents.
Layer 0 is a polygon Feature Layer.
Layer description says it records survey extent, capture date, DTM resolution and transformation models.
Layer supports JSON, GeoJSON and PBF query formats.
Layer time extent shown by the service runs from 2005 through 2022.
Layer reports Has Live Data false.
filename is an exposed provenance field.
os_ref is an exposed provenance field.
sd_flown and ed_flown are exposed survey-date fields.
pt_count and pt_spacing are exposed point-cloud sampling fields.
transform and geoid are exposed transformation provenance fields.
filepath is an exposed source-path field.
supplied and latest are exposed source/version context fields.
polygon_id is an exposed survey-feature identity field.
Layer data/schema last edit date is 13 May 2025.
Composite DTM 1m covers about 99 percent of England at 1m spatial resolution.
Composite DTM removes surface objects to model terrain surface.
The 2022 composite merges Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest best-resolution data is used.
Resampled source data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
Composite DTM 1m is supplied as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km tiles aligned to OS National Grid, metres to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Time Stamped DTM offers 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on survey and has stated vertical accuracy +/-15cm RMSE.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height DTM product for Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour forms are created from the same source data.
Both forms are supplied as 10km-by-10km tiles.
Tiles are identified by National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
Terrain 50 grid has regular 50m post spacing.
Terrain 50 contours use 10m interval standard contour polylines.
Online download is available with no registration required.
ASCII, GML and Esri shapefile tiled supply covers Great Britain.
Those tiles are arranged into 55 100km-grid folders.
Full national grid-tile supply is about 157 MB compressed.
ASCII grid heights are calculated at pixel centres.
ASCII rows run west to east with 200 pixels per row.
Height values are given to the nearest 0.1m.
ASCII header uses ncols 200 and nrows 200.
GML provides metadata including location, grid spacing and vertical reference information for the ASCII grid.
OS Terrain 50 XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard and is also provided per tile.
Per-tile metadata identifies the 10km National Grid tile reference and British National Grid coordinate reference system.
